notes: SYNTHETIC DEMO FIXTURES for the future Outlook add-in and for backend tests (src/services/pipeline/email.test.js).
Every organisation, person, domain, address and account here is fictional (.example TLD, RFC 2606). No real credentials or financial details.
Each fixture is a ready-made POST /api/analyze body plus the outcome the deterministic engine (semantic model off) must produce.
Suppliers and people referenced here exist only in data/demo-supplier-registry.json and data/demo-organisation-directory.json.

fixtures.title: Legitimate supplier invoice
fixtures.demoTalkingPoint: Known supplier, known address, DMARC pass, PDF invoice, the account on record: FraudLens stays quiet.

request.message:
Dear Accounts Payable,

Please find attached invoice INV-1182 for September deliveries, total Rs 48,250, due by 30 October. As usual, payment goes to our account ending 4491.

Kind regards,
Finance Team, ABC Supplies Ltd

fixtures.title: Reply-To differs, nothing else
fixtures.demoTalkingPoint: A different Reply-To is recorded as weak evidence - on its own it never makes an email 'dangerous'.

request.message: Your shipment MU-4471 has arrived at Port Louis and will be delivered on Thursday. Reply to this email if you need a different delivery slot.

fixtures.title: Obvious credential phishing
fixtures.demoTalkingPoint: Password request + unofficial login link + replies redirected: the email-specific actions say not to enter a password.

request.message: Your mailbox password expires today. Verify your account immediately at https://m365-login-verify.example/secure and confirm your password, or you will lose access.

fixtures.title: Supplier impersonation with changed bank details
fixtures.demoTalkingPoint: Look-alike supplier domain (suppiies), replies to Gmail, and an account that is not the one on record (****4491). Authentication PASSES - the attacker owns the look-alike domain.

request.message:
Dear Accounts Payable,

Please note our bank details have changed. Kindly settle invoice INV-1182 (Rs 48,250) to our new account ending 6789 today.

Regards,
ABC Supplies Accounts

fixtures.title: Bank-change email for a supplier with no account on record
fixtures.demoTalkingPoint: Same wording, but FraudLens holds no previous account for this supplier - so it does NOT claim the details changed (no EMAIL-06). The wording alone is still flagged.

request.message: Please note our bank details have changed. Kindly settle the attached invoice to our new account ending 6789.

fixtures.title: CEO impersonation (BEC) from a personal address
fixtures.demoTalkingPoint: The display name is the CEO from the directory, the address is Gmail, and the request is urgent, secret and skips finance.

request.message: I need you to process an urgent transfer of Rs 850,000 to a new vendor today for a confidential acquisition. Keep this confidential and don't involve finance until it closes. I'm in meetings all day, so reply by email only.

fixtures.title: Compromised real supplier mailbox
fixtures.demoTalkingPoint: SPF, DKIM and DMARC all PASS and the address is the supplier's real one - a phishing filter lets it through. FraudLens still stops it: the account is not the one on record, and the language asks for secrecy and skipping verification.

request.message: Urgent: we are being audited, so please transfer the outstanding Rs 48,250 today to our temporary account number 0045 1123 6789 instead. This is confidential - keep this between us, and there is no need to call to confirm.

fixtures.title: Conversation hijack with a look-alike domain
fixtures.demoTalkingPoint: Earlier replies came from abc-supplies.example; this one comes from abc-suppiies.example and changes the account. One fact (the look-alike sender) is scored once, corroborated by the thread check.

request.message: Further to our thread, please note our bank details have been updated. Use account ending 5521 for INV-1182.
